cases.explain: Звонок is the grammatical subject of послышался (was heard), so it is in the nominative case.

cases.translation: He was sent by Countess Lidia Ivanovna.
cases.explain: The preposition от (from/by) governs the genitive case.

cases.sentence: Написал записку к тому, от кого это зависело, и передал ___е.
cases.translation: He wrote a note to the person on whom it depended, and handed it to the princess.
cases.explain: Княгине is the indirect object of передал (handed to), which takes the dative case.
Записку is the direct object of напишите (write); feminine nouns take the -у ending in the accusative singular.

cases.sentence: Один господин, который с ___ом в руке говорил речь добровольцам.
cases.translation: A gentleman who, glass in hand, was making a speech to the volunteers.
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) governs the instrumental case.

cases.translation: Having asked about the details... concerning the young man who had applied.
cases.explain: The preposition о (about) governs the prepositional case.

reading.ru: Едва Сергей Иванович с Котовасовым успели подъехать к особенно оживленной нынче народом станции Курской железной дороги и выйдя из кареты осмотреть подъезжавшего сзади с вещами лакея, как подъехали и добровольцы на четырех извозчиках.
reading.question: What were Sergei Ivanovich and Katavasov doing as they arrived at the station?
options: Getting out of the carriage to check on the footman bringing their luggage, as volunteers arrived in cabs
reading.correct: Getting out of the carriage to check on the footman bringing their luggage, as volunteers arrived in cabs
reading.explain: As they got out to check on the footman bringing their luggage, volunteers arrived on four cabs.

reading.ru: Дамы с букетами встретили их и в сопровождении хлынувшей за ними толпы вошли в станцию.
reading.question: How were the volunteers greeted at the station?
options: By ladies with bouquets, followed by a surging crowd
reading.correct: By ladies with bouquets, followed by a surging crowd
reading.explain: Ladies with bouquets met them, and they entered the station accompanied by a crowd that surged after them.

reading.ru: «Правда, что от нас отправлено уже восемьсот. Мне не верил Мальвинский».
reading.question: How many volunteers had already been sent from Moscow, according to the princess?
reading.explain: The princess says that eight hundred had already been sent from Moscow.

reading.ru: «А какова нынешняя телеграмма? Опять разбили турок?»
reading.question: What does the latest telegram report, according to the conversation?
options: That the Turks had been defeated again
That a volunteer ship had sunk
reading.correct: That the Turks had been defeated again
reading.explain: The princess asks about the telegram, wondering if the Turks were beaten again, which Sergei Ivanovich confirms he read about.

reading.ru: «Ах, да, знаете, один молодой человек, прекрасный, просился. Не знаю, почему сделали затруднение.
reading.question: What favor does the princess ask of Sergei Ivanovich?
options: To write a note so a young man's application to volunteer would be accepted
reading.correct: To write a note so a young man's application to volunteer would be accepted
reading.explain: The princess mentions a fine young man who applied but met with difficulty, and asks Sergei Ivanovich to write a note on his behalf.

reading.ru: «Вы знаете, граф Вронский, известный, едет с этим поездом», сказала княгиня с торжествующей и многозначительной улыбкой
reading.question: What news does the princess share about Vronsky?
options: That the well-known Count Vronsky is traveling on this very train
reading.correct: That the well-known Count Vronsky is traveling on this very train
reading.explain: The princess tells Sergei Ivanovich, with a triumphant smile, that the famous Count Vronsky is traveling on this train.

reading.ru: «Послужить за веру, за человечество, за братьев наших!» — все возвышая голос, говорил господин.
reading.question: What does the gentleman with the glass urge the volunteers to do?
options: Serve for the faith, for humanity, and for their brothers
reading.correct: Serve for the faith, for humanity, and for their brothers
reading.explain: Raising his voice, the gentleman with the glass calls on them to serve for the faith, humanity, and their brothers.

reading.ru: «На великое дело благословляет вас матушка Москва! Живио!» — громко и слезно заключил он.
reading.question: How does the gentleman's speech to the volunteers end?
options: With "Mother Moscow blesses you for this great cause! Zhivio!"
With a toast to the tsar
reading.correct: With "Mother Moscow blesses you for this great cause! Zhivio!"
reading.explain: He concludes loudly and tearfully, saying Mother Moscow blesses them for the great cause, followed by cries of "Zhivio!"

reading.ru: Так вы жену мою увидите. Я писал ей, но вы прежде увидите.
reading.question: What does Stepan Arkadyich ask Sergei Ivanovich to tell his wife?
options: That he was seen and that he has been appointed to a joint commission
That he lost all his money
reading.correct: That he was seen and that he has been appointed to a joint commission
reading.explain: Stepan Arkadyich asks Sergei Ivanovich, who will see his wife before his own letter arrives, to tell her he was seen and that he was appointed to a joint commission.

reading.ru: «Не могу видеть этих кружек спокойно, пока у меня есть деньги», — сказал он.
reading.question: What does Stepan Arkadyich say as he gives money to a collector?
options: That he cannot look calmly at collection boxes while he still has money
That he has no money to give
That he prefers to give food instead
reading.correct: That he cannot look calmly at collection boxes while he still has money
reading.explain: Giving a five-ruble note to a lady with a collection box, he says he cannot look at such boxes calmly while he still has money.

reading.ru: Он не только едет сам, но эскадрон ведет на свой счет.
reading.question: What special sacrifice does Vronsky make in going to war?
options: He not only goes himself but also equips a squadron at his own expense
He donates his house to refugees
He pays only for the volunteers' uniforms
reading.correct: He not only goes himself but also equips a squadron at his own expense
reading.explain: The princess notes that Vronsky not only goes himself but is leading a squadron at his own expense.

reading.ru: Выйдя на платформу, Вронский, молча пропустив мать, скрылся в отделении вагона.
reading.question: What does Vronsky do as he steps onto the platform?
options: He silently lets his mother go ahead and disappears into a train compartment
He gives a speech to the crowd
reading.correct: He silently lets his mother go ahead and disappears into a train compartment
reading.explain: Stepping onto the platform, Vronsky silently lets his mother pass ahead and disappears into a compartment of the train car.
